clue.text: It became apparent, then it became a mother or a father?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for finally understanding something, when realisation clicks into place

definitions.text: then it became a mother or a father?
definitions.meaning: read literally: a woman named Penny gave birth, 'dropped' being a farmyard word for giving birth

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something becoming clear and then becoming a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped' is used of animals giving birth, so a person called Penny who 'dropped' became a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes the moment understanding suddenly arrives, so something has become apparent.

clue.text: Pub's opening, soon to host the nation's heroes

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of 'Pub's'
a host has guests inside, so the word for soon takes the other piece into its middle

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub is about to welcome the country's celebrated figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to host' means the word for soon is split open to take in the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is, figuratively, the collective group of a country's most revered and honoured figures.

clue.text: See 23
Awkward adding jewels to one's booty

indicators.note: adding one thing to another sets the jewels after the bottom in a charade

parts.note: booty is slang for the backside, as is bum in British English
bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A clumsy person decorates their bottom with gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booty' looks like plunder but is slang for the bottom; BUM is British slang for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, inept and blundering behaviour is described as bumbling.

clue.text: Losing seat

definitions.meaning: trailing in a contest, adverb or adjective of being in arrears
the part of the body one sits on, the bottom

explanation.definitionFit: Being in arrears in a match, and a polite word for the buttocks one sits upon.

clue.text: Padding delicate area, knotted rags — ribbed fabric

indicators.note: padding fills the inside of something, so the delicate area gets stuffed with the other letters

parts.note: the groin is a sensitive part of the body

indicators.note: knotted string is twisted out of order, so these letters are tangled up

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs tied-up rags around a sensitive part of the body, beside a mention of ribbed cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Padding' reads as part of the surface's stuffing, but it means the shuffled letters from 'knotted' go inside the delicate area.
explanation.definitionFit: Grosgrain is a heavy corded silk or ribbon with pronounced transverse ribs.

clue.text: See 17 across
In money, pound taken to entertain maiden fair? Absolutely not!

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay is placed within the word for money

parts.note: dough is slang for cash

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means having them within, so the scrambled word takes in the maiden letter
to pound something is to batter it out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a mela is a South Asian fair or festival

explanation.surface: Someone at a fair thinks about money and a pound being spent on a young woman, then scoffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' rearranges the letters to NTAKE; 'to entertain' takes in M; 'In' places all of it inside the money word. MELA is a South Asian fair.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is a sarcastic, emphatic refusal or dismissal, as strong as saying no way.

clue.text: Parasite was a parliamentary leader, said Spooner?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two pieces exchange their initial sounds

parts.note: with 'leader', was a leader means led
a parliamentary chamber is a house, such as the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A query whether a bloodsucker once headed parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'was a parliamentary leader' gives LED HOUSE; swap the first sounds to get the scalp pest.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect lives on the human scalp and feeds on blood, a classic parasite.

clue.text: Minister detailed one side of the story?

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a rector is a parish minister or priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman gave a one-sided account in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'thorough' but means lose the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Recto is the right-hand page of a book, one side of a leaf that a story is printed on.

clue.text: Trouble brewing at first, plant in a stew perhaps?

parts.note: pother is an old word for fuss or commotion

indicators.note: only the opening letter of 'brewing' is used

explanation.surface: Trouble begins to brew, and a plant ends up in the casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-herb is any leafy plant grown to flavour or be cooked in soups and stews.

clue.text: Point covered by this or otherwise, to be concise

indicators.note: a thing covered by another is inside it, so the point sits within the rearranged letters
otherwise means in another way, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A debating remark that a point is covered by one thing or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' shuffles THIS OR into ISHORT; N goes in after I.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to sum things up briefly, meaning to put it concisely or in a word.

clue.text: Season as seasona, it's reported?

indicators.note: something reported is said out loud, so the clue words are judged by their sound

parts.note: seasona is seasonal with no L, which said out loud is the festive word

explanation.surface: A misprinted word for seasonal, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seasona' is 'seasonal' missing its L: that is, 'no L', which sounds like the festive word.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the festive season.

clue.text: Poor character recalled in rogue

indicators.note: something rogue is wayward and out of control, so these letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An impoverished figure is remembered as a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' looks like a noun but is an adjective signalling the rearrangement of RECALLED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine is a poor kitchen drudge before the ball, the archetypal poor character.

clue.text: See 22
Trying jerks in family — something positive about it?

definitions.note: making sharp tugs in an attempt to shift something

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the positive principle wraps round the family

parts.note: yang is the positive, active principle in Chinese philosophy
kin means relatives, one's family

explanation.surface: Tiresome idiots in the family, and is there anything good to say about it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying jerks' reads as annoying people but means giving tugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull with a sudden sharp tug, so giving such tugs.

clue.text: Where one may be taught a lesson with ice down jockstrap, might you say?

definitions.text: Where one may be taught a lesson

indicators.note: a hint that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: ice in an athletic support chills the genitals: cool

explanation.surface: A fee-paying establishment, and an unpleasant prank in the changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privates cool' said out loud is the fee-paying educational establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee-paying school is a place where pupils are taught their lessons.

clue.text: Best honours, we hear, for Spanish fighters

indicators.note: the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: pick means the best, and adores means honours or worships

explanation.surface: A boast about top awards for Spanish combatants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick adores' spoken sounds like the bullring horsemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Picadors are mounted lancers who fight bulls in a Spanish bullfight.

clue.text: Perfumed lorry carrying odorous muck around, initially

indicators.note: a lorry carries a load inside, so the vehicle word holds the initials

parts.note: artic is British short for an articulated lorry

indicators.note: the first letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: A truck transports smelly manure about, yet the result is fragrant.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is the British name for an articulated lorry; 'carrying' puts the initials inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aromatic has a pleasant, spicy scent, so it smells perfumed.

clue.text: Plaything Aladdin, perhaps, has to avoid

parts.note: Aladdin rubbed the lamp to summon the genie, so he is an example of one who rubs
to duck something is to dodge it

explanation.surface: Aladdin must steer clear of a toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aladdin, perhaps' looks like an example of the toy; it is an example of someone who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow bath toy is the classic example of a child's plaything.

clue.text: Note in plain song

indicators.note: the note sits inside the word for plain

parts.note: bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement
la is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note in plainsong, the unaccompanied church chant.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or slow sentimental song.

clue.text: Track player, runner and winger

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, and a river runs
a jay is a bird, a winged creature

explanation.surface: A sports team of athletes: someone on the track, a runner and a winger.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner for a river and winger for a bird are crossword conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey plays tracks of recorded music.

clue.text: Film Keith clued cryptically?

indicators.note: says the title itself is to be read as a cryptic instruction whose result is the name in the clue

parts.note: the name is a run of letters spanning the last three words of the film's title

explanation.surface: A man named Keith is the subject of a cryptic clue for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the title as an instruction: take some of the last three words of the title, and the run across them spells KEITH.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1959 Billy Wilder comedy with Marilyn Monroe is a classic Hollywood picture.

clue.text: Swimming fish, or else biting insects

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters swim into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning: swim, fish, or the insects will bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming fish' looks like the definition but 'Swimming' shuffles FISH OR ELSE.
explanation.definitionFit: These large flies, the females of which suck blood, bite horses, cattle and people.

clue.text: Whitish gallery hasn't a range of colours

parts.note: pale means light or whitish in colour

indicators.note: lacking something means it is removed, so the gallery loses a letter

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A pale gallery lacks colourful variety.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous London art gallery; without its A it gives TTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's palette, and by extension the selection of hues used, is a range of colours.

clue.text: Model I love in performance

indicators.note: these letters sit within the word for performance

parts.note: a drama is a play or performance
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A model declares her love while performing.
explanation.walkthrough: IO goes inside DRAMA after DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scale model of a scene.

clue.text: Muse of Homer, a touch inspiring?

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the answer is drawn in from within these words

explanation.surface: A goddess who inspired Homer, even just a little?
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' fits the Muse in the surface but means taking in letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato was the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Impressive responsibility of the police

definitions.meaning: taking suspects into custody is the police's job

explanation.definitionFit: Striking enough to grab attention, and taking suspects into custody, a core police duty.
